subject: Smoothed trend line on top of nested line plots

messages.author: d994cff5897faec8
messages.subject: Smoothed trend line on top of nested line plots
parts:
The attached data set is (a cut-down version of) a series of profiling
runs of some software I'm developing. I've come up with two ways to
look at it:

ggplot(prune, aes(x=trial, y=count)) + facet_wrap(~ patch, nrow=1) + geom_line()
ggplot(prune, aes(x=patch, y=count)) + geom_point(alpha=0.5) +
stat_smooth(aes(group=1)) + opts(axis.text.x=theme_text(angle=10,
hjust=1))

The second one shows the overall trend better, but the first one
reveals structure within each profiling run that the second one loses.
What I'd like to produce is a combination of the two, basically
replacing the geom_point(alpha=0.5) from the second with the lines
drawn by the first. How might I do that?

Thanks,
zw

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: Smoothed trend line on top of nested line plots
parts:
It's a bit hacky, but here's one possibility:

ggplot(prune, aes(x=patch, y=count)) +
scale_x_discrete() +
geom_line(aes(x = as.numeric(patch) + trial / 100 - 0.5, group = patch)) +
stat_smooth(aes(group=1)) +
opts(axis.text.x=theme_text(angle=30, hjust=1))

Hadley
